subject: Feasibility: combined student + finance addendum for pilot (FERPA + GLBA)
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightbridge-district.org>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightbridge-district.org, talvarez@brightbridge-district.org
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot request — can we combine FERPA + GLBA language for student-finance use case?

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our team liked the latency profile and the ability to pin model versions for the campus finance reconciliation workflow. We have a short pilot we'd like to run (quarterly meal program reconciliation plus student billing cross-checks) and procurement asked me to check feasibility on the privacy side.

Questions up front:
- Can you support a single addendum that covers both FERPA-sensitive student records and GLBA-sensitive financial records for the district?
- Will Redwood commit to US-only subprocessors and data residency for the pilot?
- Do you have an initial draft of an addendum we can share with counsel?

Attached is our security questionnaire (BrightBridge_Security_Q_2027.pdf). Happy to set a call if that's easier. Our counsel (Tomás) is cc'd.

Best,
Jordan Ellis
Director of IT, BrightBridge Charter District
Procurement: procurement@brightbridge-district.org

Attachment: BrightBridge_Security_Q_2027.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightbridge-district.org>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — can we combine FERPA + GLBA language for student-finance use case?

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the questionnaire. Short answers here while I pull in legal/compliance:

- Combined addendum: yes, we can draft a combined vertical addendum that addresses both FERPA and GLBA obligations for the pilot. We typically carve the scoped data categories and processing activities into the addendum so the obligations map to each dataset.
- US-only subprocessors & residency: supported as an option for Dedicated or Private deployments; for hosted we can offer routing and subprocessor constraints but would need to confirm with ops (I’ll confirm below).
- Draft addendum: attaching a first-pass combined addendum draft (redwood_combined-addendum-draft_v1.pdf) for you and Tomás to review. It’s intentionally conservative on retention and access controls — we can relax certain controls for Dedicated.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick call with you + Tomás + our compliance lead (Mina) to walk the addendum and security answers, 2) indicate whether you require Dedicated/Private for the pilot or if hosted with residency constraints is acceptable. I’m flexible for a 30-min call Wed or Thu.

Action: Jordan — can you share the pilot scope (expected PII/PHI fields, volume, and retention window) before the call? That will let Mina tailor the obligations.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0128

Attachment: redwood_combined-addendum-draft_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightbridge-district.org>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, talvarez@brightbridge-district.org
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 13:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — can we combine FERPA + GLBA language for student-finance use case?

Jordan/Tomás — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear ask. A few compliance notes from legal/security perspective:

1) Scope & Definitions: The addendum draft Lauren shared separates the data categories (Student Educational Records = FERPA; Customer financial data = GLBA). That separation is important because retention, lawful processing bases, and disclosure rules differ.

2) Subprocessors: We can agree to US-only subprocessors for the pilot. For hosted accounts, we can include a subprocessor residency clause and a 30-day notification window for changes. If you require contractual pre-approval of each subprocessor, that is possible but increases procurement lead time.

3) Data residency: For strict residency (no cross-border replication), we recommend either Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in a US region or our Private deployment. Hosted can be configured with region routing but cannot guarantee zero replication for some analytics/backup flows without Dedicated/Private.

4) Security controls: We can tighten retention defaults for the pilot (30 days) and enable KMIP-backed key separation for the district on Dedicated/Private. We will also include audit log export for the pilot period.

5) Counsel review items: Tomás, the main negotiation points will likely be 1) definitions mapping, 2) breach notification timelines (we propose 72 hours for security incidents), and 3) liability caps for regulated data.

I can join the call to run through the technical controls. I suggest Wed 1/20 at 10:00 PT or Thu 1/21 at 09:00 PT.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
From: Tomás Alvarez <talvarez@brightbridge-district.org>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightbridge-district.org>, procurement@brightbridge-district.org, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — can we combine FERPA + GLBA language for student-finance use case?

Lauren / Mina — thanks for the quick responses and draft addendum. A few clarifying items from counsel: 

- We prefer contractual pre-approval of subprocessors for this pilot. Can you provide your current subprocessors list and the last three months of change history?
- For breach notification, 48 hours would be preferable given regulated data crossing educational and financial boundaries. Can Redwood commit to 48 hours or provide escalation options?
- On liability, BrightBridge requests carveouts that preserve recovery for students and families affected by data misuse. We expect a negotiation here — please flag which clauses are most negotiable.

Also, we’d like to keep retention at 90 days for reconciliation needs unless operation cost reasons force a shorter window. Please flag operational tradeoffs for 90 vs 30 days.

We can do the call Wed 1/20 at 10:00 PT. I’ll have our procurement manager on the line.

Regards,
Tomás Alvarez
District Counsel, BrightBridge Charter District
talvarez@brightbridge-district.org
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Tomás Alvarez <talvarez@brightbridge-district.org>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@brightbridge-district.org>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, procurement@brightbridge-district.org
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — can we combine FERPA + GLBA language for student-finance use case?

Tomás/Jordan — thanks for confirming the call time. Quick reply ahead of the meeting with the items you requested:

- Subprocessor list + change log: Vivek — I’ve asked ops to share a current list and change log; we’ll put that in the Drive folder before the call.
- Breach notification: Mina and I discussed escalation paths — for security incidents impacting regulated student or financial data we can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours and a written incident report within 5 business days. We’ll surface an SLA exception for 48-hour initial notice into the addendum draft for the pilot.
- Retention tradeoffs: Operationally, 90 days increases storage and exposure but is reasonable for reconciliation. For hosted accounts 90 days is doable with a modest uplift; Dedicated/Private gives more flexibility and lower incremental cost per GB. Mina will bring expected cost delta figures to the call.

Next steps for the call: 1) run through the redwood_combined-addendum-draft_v1.pdf, 2) review subprocessor list (Drive link), 3) agree on retention and breach timeline for pilot, 4) procurement to confirm whether they need pre-approval vs notification.

See you on Wed 1/20 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
